import html # Pre‑defined HTML template with placeholders for the event details. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}

{event_title}

Date: {event_date}

{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def create_event_invitation(e_title: str, e_description: str, e_date: str, e_notes: str) -> str: """ Produce a sanitized HTML invitation for an event. Args: e_title: The name or heading of the event. e_description: A detailed description that may contain newlines and user‑supplied formatting. e_date: The scheduled date of the event. e_notes: Additional instructions or information from the user. Returns: A string containing a fully escaped HTML representation of the invitation. All user input is passed through html.escape to prevent XSS and ensure well‑formed output (CWE-707). Raises: TypeError: If any argument is not a string. """ # Validate types if not all(isinstance(arg, str) for arg in (e_title, e_description, e_date, e_notes)): raise TypeError("All arguments must be strings") # Escape user supplied content escaped_title = html.escape(e_title, quote=True) escaped_description = html.escape(e_description, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') escaped_date = html.escape(e_date, quote=True) escaped_notes = html.escape(e_notes, quote=False).replace('\n', '
') # Format the template with sanitized values invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=escaped_title, event_date=escaped_date, event_description=escaped_description, additional_notes=escaped_notes ) return invitation_html
